RoboLedger's ledger now stands on its own, and its statements became tools you work in rather than pages you read.

1.1.0 is the first feature release since 1.0.0. It gathers everything shipped since then (August 4, 2026) — thirty-one patch releases, each with its own changelog, none of which told the whole story. The through-line: a graph no longer needs QuickBooks to have books, the surfaces where you read numbers can now be folded, sorted, compared and scrolled without losing your place, and RoboLedger gained a public front door.

## Key features

**A ledger that stands on its own**

- **Native chart of accounts** — a graph with no chart now starts from a template picker, with the entity's legal form (corporation, LLC, partnership) driving the equity mapping, instead of waiting on an import. Removing a QuickBooks connection asks which you mean: _disconnect_ (revivable on re-authorization) or _sever and go native_, keeping the chart QuickBooks created as the graph's own.
- **Journal** — `/ledger/transactions` became `/ledger/journal`, and the old address redirects. The journal reads entries directly, so it shows what a transaction list structurally could not: entries with no parent transaction — every depreciation, amortization and accrual a period close posts. Filter by status, entry type and source; the schedule that generated an entry is named on its row; unbalanced entries are badged. Source Transactions stays beside it as a second view, deliberately not merged.
- **Mercury bank feed** — setup, OAuth callback, and a _Post to account_ picker on bank lines in the Inbox: classify a line, then approve it. The picker never touches the amount or the bank leg. **The provider is gated on the API and is off in production until Mercury's compliance review clears**; until then the connections marketplace does not list it.

**Statements you can work in**

- **Live Statements** — columns carry their dates (_As of Sep 18, 2026_, or _Jan 1 – Sep 18, 2026_ for a flow statement) and read prior → current, left to right. Sections fold onto their subtotals, with expand and collapse all, and a _Show change_ toggle adds signed dollar and percent columns.
- **Block Explorer on a long series** — the statement and metric grids were rebuilt for a standing monthly series. Line-item labels stay pinned as you scroll, the title and controls stay put, row backgrounds span the full width, and headers read _Jul 2024_ with the full window on hover. A series longer than a year opens on its trailing twelve months, with _All_ one click away. Statements fold here the same way, and a folded section stays folded when the window changes.
- **Validation you can read** — a three-state badge (_passed_, _failed_, _not validated_) on the close and, new, on Live Statements, which previously ran no validation. A statement with no rules reads as not validated, never as a pass. A finding raised in many periods now groups to one line per kind with a period count — a 25-month cash flow statement shows three lines instead of sixty-five.
- **A close gate that explains itself** — blockers read as plain instructions rather than internal codes, including the one that matters most: scheduled entries promoted but never drafted, which a close would otherwise silently omit.
- **Refresh in place** on Plan, the Explorer and Live Statements, with a last-fetched label. The populated view stays mounted while it reloads.

**Reports**

- **Ask about this report** — the RoboSystems operator on the report's own graph, anchored on the report on screen, paid from the graph's credits with no key to enter. Read-only: the close, schedules and entries keep their own gated flows.
- **Rendered from the Tavi** — the report page loads the report's compiled standards-form model, falling back to the holon for a copy shared before it existed, and offers a _Tavi (JSON)_ download.
- **Cross-graph share controls** — on a report received from another graph: block the sender (with a private note never shown to them), delete your copy, and review or lift blocks at `/reports/blocked-senders`. None of it waits on the sender's publication status.

**One way of doing things**

- **Filter bars** — seven list pages each hand-rolled their filter row, and the copies had drifted apart. They now share one compact bar, one label style and one control size, with a single segmented control replacing four different looks for "pick one". Trial Balance's view switch became _Chart of Accounts | US-GAAP_; a toggle labelled on both sides never said which side was on.
- **Click-to-sort** on Trial Balance and Entities. A third click returns to the natural order — on the Trial Balance that is the chart of accounts' own, which no column sort reproduces. Sorting is offered only where the whole list is in hand, not on a capped fetch like the Journal or Inbox.
- **Names without the prefix** — statements are titled _Balance Sheet — Classified_, not _rs-gaap — Balance Sheet — Classified_, in the Explorer's rail and above the statement itself.

**Connect and learn**

- **Paste a URL, not an install** — connecting Claude to your books is now your ledger's MCP endpoint and an API key, replacing the npm bridge and its config file.
- **Docs and a blog on roboledger.ai** — product documentation at `/docs` and a `/blog`, both rendered from the shared content catalog, with guide links on the app pages they explain and in the user menu.
- **One account home** — account settings, sign-in methods, API keys and graph creation live on the RoboSystems login home. RoboLedger hands you off and keeps your place; the detours open in a new tab so a half-filled form survives.

## Changed and removed

- **The SEC connection is gone from Connections.** It was already unreachable in every deployed environment. SEC filings still arrive nightly in the shared SEC repository; only the per-graph connection went.
- **Live Statements column order changed** to prior → current. The numbers are unchanged; if you reconcile against a screenshot, the columns have swapped sides.
- Connections copy no longer says data sources import "automatically". Every sync is on demand, as it always was.

## Bug fixes

- The search magnifier floated outside its field on every list page.
- Business rules no longer render in failure colors. A block whose every rule passed announced "10 Error" in red — severity is a property of the rule, not something that happened.
- A failed Live Statements render shows a readable message with a link to the fix, not the raw error envelope.
- Table header cells sit in a row. Every table put `<th>` directly inside `<thead>`, which is invalid HTML and a hydration mismatch for any server-rendered table.
- Charts are readable in dark mode; prose table headers regained their dark-mode contrast; the landing page stopped overflowing on mobile.
- An unfinished OAuth sign-in can be resumed from the connection card.

## Platform and infrastructure

- **`@robosystems/client` 0.6 → 1.17** — the SDK's first stable major, adopted at its call sites, and the minors that followed it. **`@robosystems/core` 0.5.7 → 0.9.4**. **`@robosystems/report-components` 0.3.1 → 0.6.0**, which changes how report statements render. Next.js 16.1 → 16.3; Node 24.19 base image.
- **Deploying 1.1.0** — requires RoboSystems API **v1.12.0 or later**; deploy the API first. Against an older API the Mercury and Tavi surfaces fall back quietly, but the chart template picker errors. No CloudFormation changes ride this release and nothing needs setting before the deploy: the two new variables, `NEXT_PUBLIC_DOCS_CATALOG_URL` and `NEXT_PUBLIC_BLOG_CATALOG_URL`, are optional overrides with built-in defaults.
- **CI** — review, tagging and the composite actions now come from the shared workflows in the `robosystems` repository. Release deployments are dispatch-only, the production approval gate runs ahead of tests, and the Docker Hub build runs alongside the deploy rather than on its critical path.
- **Dependencies** — Dependabot covers npm, GitHub Actions and the Node base image; outstanding dependency advisories were cleared.
- AWS bootstrap moved to the backend repository (`just bootstrap`); this repo's `bootstrap.sh` was removed.
